questions.prompt: Identify two components of a mind map.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept any two: central node/idea/topic, nodes/sub-nodes, branches/connecting lines, keywords/text, images/icons, colours.

questions.prompt: Which of these is not an operating system?
questions.markSchemeHint: C) Office (1 mark).

questions.scenarioContext: A Human Computer Interface (HCI) is designed to manipulate numeric data.
questions.prompt: Which digital platform would be used?
questions.markSchemeHint: Spreadsheet (software).

questions.prompt: Identify one user interaction method other than touch that could be used on a HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept mouse, keyboard, voice, gesture, stylus/pen, gaze/eye tracking, or game controller/joystick.

questions.prompt: Which of these is not a numeric data type?
questions.markSchemeHint: A) Boolean (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Which validation tool would be used to check that data has been entered into a field on a form?
questions.markSchemeHint: Presence check.

questions.prompt: Identify one data verification tool.
questions.markSchemeHint: Double entry or visual/manual checking (proofreading).

questions.prompt: Identify two primary data collection methods.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept any two: questionnaires/surveys, interviews, focus groups, observations, polls, experiments/sensors.

questions.prompt: Link the type of malware to the correct description. (You will only use two types of malware to complete this task.)
matchingLeft: A standalone program that replicates itself
questions.markSchemeHint: Worm -> A standalone program that replicates itself (1); Spyware -> Collects user log-in details (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Data theft can occur when data is in transit.
questions.prompt: Identify one other state when data theft could occur.
questions.markSchemeHint: At rest (or in storage / in use).

questions.prompt: What does RFID stand for?
questions.markSchemeHint: Radio Frequency Identification.

questions.prompt: Identify the legislation that relates to the protection of an image.
questions.markSchemeHint: Copyright, Designs and Patents Act (1988).

questions.scenarioContext: An animal charity is organising a discovery trail competition which will last for three weeks. Painted statues of dogs will be placed in different locations of a town for people to find. To take part people have to register using a HCI on a mobile app and pay an entry charge. Each person who registers is allocated an entry number.
questions.prompt: Data is entered to register on the mobile app using a HCI. What is meant by the term 'data'?
questions.markSchemeHint: Raw, unprocessed facts, figures, symbols, or characters (1) that have no meaning or context on their own (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Data validation has been used on the HCI for the animal charity mobile app registration screen.
questions.prompt: Describe how the data type check and input mask can be used to reduce data entry errors on the registration screen.
questions.markSchemeHint: Data type check (2): ensures only the correct type of characters are entered (e.g., only numbers in phone/payment or letters in name), rejecting invalid characters. Input mask (2): forces data into a predefined pattern/format (e.g., UK postcode LL00 0LL or date DD/MM/YYYY) to prevent formatting mistakes.

questions.scenarioContext: The charity has stored details about each entrant on a network drive. A backup of this data is stored on a USB flash drive.
questions.prompt: Identify two characteristics of a USB flash drive that make it suitable to store the backup.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept any two: portable/small (can be taken off-site), durable/solid-state (no moving parts), relatively cheap, fast read/write speeds, sufficient storage capacity, plug-and-play compatibility.

questions.scenarioContext: Animal charity entrants' personal data backup.
questions.prompt: What is identity theft?
questions.markSchemeHint: When someone steals/obtains another person's personal details without permission (1) and uses them to impersonate them or commit fraud/financial crime (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Logical prevention measures will be used to increase the protection of the entrants' data stored on the USB flash drive.
questions.prompt: Explain how two-factor authentication (2FA) and encryption could be used by the animal charity to keep the data stored on the USB flash drive secure.
questions.markSchemeHint: 2FA (2): requires two separate forms of verification (e.g., password + one-time code/biometric) so a stolen password alone cannot unlock the backup. Encryption (2): scrambles the data into unreadable ciphertext so if the USB drive is lost or stolen, unauthorised users cannot read it without the decryption key.

questions.scenarioContext: The mobile app has a HCI. Part of the HCI is the registration screen for the competition.
questions.prompt: Identify one hardware resource that should be considered when designing the registration screen.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept display/screen size/resolution, memory (RAM), processor (CPU), storage, battery life, or input hardware (touchscreen).

questions.scenarioContext: The animal charity could use Desktop Publishing (DTP) software to create the visualisation diagram of the registration screen.
questions.prompt: Explain two advantages to the animal charity of using DTP software to create the visualisation diagram.
questions.markSchemeHint: 2 marks each (point + explanation): precise layout/positioning using grids/frames; built-in templates/shapes/text boxes; easy to edit/amend and share digitally with stakeholders; professional appearance.

questions.scenarioContext: Animal charity discovery trail mobile app registration screen.
questions.prompt: Explain how using the HCI on a mobile app will impact on the design of the HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark for mobile design constraint + 1 mark for design adaptation: smaller screen requires simple/uncluttered layout and readable fonts; touchscreen requires larger finger-friendly buttons/spacing; portrait orientation / responsive layout; limited scrolling.

questions.scenarioContext: Entrants must input their name, address and contact details when using the registration screen. Payment details are accessed by clicking a button on the registration screen.
questions.prompt:
Create a visualisation diagram to plan the content for the registration screen.
Marks will be awarded for: content; layout.
questions.markSchemeHint: Up to 4 marks Content (charity title/logo, input fields for Name, Address, Contact Details/email/phone, 'Payment Details' button, annotations for colours/fonts/house style) and up to 4 marks Layout (clear mobile screen frame, logical top-to-bottom form flow, clean alignment and visual hierarchy).

questions.scenarioContext: The HCI registration screen is used by entrants to input their name, address and contact details and must be tested.
questions.prompt: Identify two examples of valid test data that the animal charity could use.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two concrete, realistic valid inputs matching the fields (e.g., 'Sam Smith' for name, '14 High Street' or 'PE1 2AB' for address/postcode, 'sam@email.com' or '07700900123' for contact details).

questions.scenarioContext: Testing the animal charity registration screen.
questions.prompt: Describe how invalid (erroneous) test data could be used to test the HCI registration screen.
questions.markSchemeHint: Entering data of the wrong type/format (e.g., numbers in Name or missing '@' in email) (1) to check that validation rules reject it and display an appropriate error message (1).

questions.scenarioContext: As entrants find each statue they use another part of the mobile app HCI to enter details about the statue found.
questions.prompt: Identify two digital devices that could be used by the entrants to enter the statue details.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept any two portable devices suitable for a mobile app: smartphone, tablet, smartwatch.

questions.scenarioContext: The entrants can use touch to interact with the HCI on the mobile app.
questions.prompt: Describe one disadvantage to the entrants of using touch to interact with the HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: e.g., difficult in wet/cold outdoor weather (gloves/rain on screen); small buttons lead to accidental taps/typing errors; harder for users with motor/visual impairments; screen glare/smudges outdoors.

questions.scenarioContext:
An example of the statue details is shown below:
• Entry number: DT124
• When found: 02/09/2025
• Statue ID: 25
• Location: 42 The High Street
questions.prompt: Complete the table to show the data types that are used when entering the details about the statue. Justify your choice.
questions.markSchemeHint: 3 marks per row (1 mark data type + 2 marks contextual justification): Entry number -> Alphanumeric/Text (contains both letters DT and numbers 124); When found -> Date (stores day/month/year in DD/MM/YYYY format for sorting/validation); Statue ID -> Integer/Numeric (whole number 25 with no decimals, allows numeric validation/sorting; also accept Text/Alphanumeric if justified as identifier not used in calculations).

questions.prompt:
Discuss the suitability of the animal charity using a digital presentation to communicate this information.

In your answer you must consider:
• the purpose of the digital presentation;
• the advantages and disadvantages to the animal charity of using the digital presentation.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 9-mark Level of Response (L1: 1–3, L2: 4–6, L3: 7–9). Cover purpose (inform/engage attendees at the live auction event, showcase statue photos, celebrate trail winners and funds raised), advantages (multimedia/images/charts make results engaging, easy to display on large screen to whole audience, quick to edit/update totals), disadvantages (requires projector/screen/power, tech failure risk, time/skill to design well, audience can't easily take a copy home without sharing), and a reasoned conclusion on suitability.
